page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.xlarge is a general-purpose instance type built on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized on the KVM hypervisor, the server provides 8 dedicated virtual CPU cores paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This yields a consistent memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU, matching standard enterprise balance requirements for multi-threaded workloads without compute oversubscription.

The instance configuration omits bundled local storage, meaning all operational persistent data relies on external cloud block storage attachments. It provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not contain discrete GPU accelerators. Furthermore, hardware instruction flags such as Advanced Vector Extensions and cryptographic acceleration suites are reported as unavailable, indicating baseline compute capabilities centered on conventional integer and system execution.

Because compute resources are dedicated rather than burstable, the instance delivers stable execution profiles suitable for predictable medium-scale workloads. Cost efficiency derives from resource density rather than raw acceleration, making it an appropriate fit for standard web servers, backend API hosting, relational database replicas, and enterprise business applications that do not require specialized hardware accelerators.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance designed around the x86_64 architecture and managed by the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server provides dedicated compute allocations, avoiding performance fluctuations common in shared or burstable environments. The platform includes no local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for operating systems and data retention, and features zero dedicated GPU accelerators. Advanced vector extensions, cryptographic acceleration flags, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included in the provisioned environment. With its balanced allocation of processor and memory capacity, ecs.m1.xlarge is structured to support stable, predictable enterprise utility tasks such as mid-sized web serving, application middleware, background processing workers, and standard database services where high-density memory or specialized hardware acceleration is not required.
